page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor platform. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor featuring 12 physical cores and 24 virtual vCPUs through hyper-threading. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include bundled local ephemeral storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for disk access and providing an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

The x86_64 processor architecture includes an instruction set with AVX, AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES-NI, FMA, and BMI2 capabilities, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. Benchmark evaluations reveal relatively weak single-core processing speeds and lower throughput in single-threaded compression tests like Gzip. However, the instance exhibits middle-tier, average performance across multi-core tests, including PassMark CPU routines, software compilation via Clang, ray tracing, image processing, and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression.

Memory bandwidth measurements achieve 90.15 GB/sec for uncached large block reads, though synthetic memory benchmarking places overall memory latency and speed in the lower quartile. In real-world application benchmarks, the server delivers 16.81 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 13.07 GB/sec in static web serving. Given its resource profile, ecs.g5.6xlarge offers practical resource density for general enterprise workloads, web serving fleets, build servers, and middleware platforms that require steady multi-core execution rather than high single-thread clock rates.

Built on x86_64 architecture with support for AVX-512 instructions, the instance includes no local storage or GPU hardware, operating with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
